cor-ci-flat-agreement.title: The flat prior reproduces the frequentist sets
cor-ci-flat-agreement.title_html: The flat prior reproduces the frequentist sets
cor-ci-flat-agreement.html: Let rank(X)=p<n, SSE>0, and let the prior be 𝛃π(β,σ2)∝1/σ2. Then the credible interval (a), the region (b), the predictive interval (c) and the interval for σ2 (d) of @thm-ci-bayes-credible are, respectively, the t interval of @thm-ci-estimable-interval, the confidence ellipsoid of @thm-ci-ellipsoid, the prediction interval of @thm-ci-prediction-interval and the interval of @prp-ci-sigma.

cor-ci-shadows.title: Shadows of the confidence ellipsoid
cor-ci-shadows.html: For every a∈Rq, the projection of E(Y) onto the line spanned by a is the interval 𝛟𝛟𝛟a⊤ϕ^ ± qFα(q,n−r) se(a⊤ϕ^),se(a⊤ϕ^)=sa⊤Wa, and E(Y) is the intersection of the slabs 𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟{ϕ0:|a⊤ϕ^−a⊤ϕ0|≤qFαse(a⊤ϕ^)} over all a. Hence, with probability exactly 1−α, every one of these intervals contains 𝛃a⊤Λ⊤β.

def-ci-band.title: Simultaneous confidence band
def-ci-band.html: Let S⊆C(X⊤) be a set of regressor vectors. Random functions ℓ(x)=ℓ(x;Y) and u(x)=u(x;Y) form a 1−α simultaneous confidence band for the regression function over S if 𝛃𝛃Prβ,σ2{ℓ(x)≤x⊤β≤u(x)  for every x∈S} ≥ 1−α for every 𝛃(β,σ2).

def-ci-confidence-set.title: Confidence set
def-ci-confidence-set.html: Let 𝛃θ=g(β,σ2) be a quantity with values in a set Θ. A confidence set for θ with confidence level 1−α is a rule that assigns to each data vector y a subset C(y)⊆Θ, such that 𝛃Prβ,σ2{θ∈C(Y)} ≥ 1−α for every 𝛃β∈Rp and σ2>0. The left side is the coverage probability at 𝛃(β,σ2). The set is exact if the coverage equals 1−α at every parameter value. When C(y) is an interval it is a confidence interval.

def-ci-credible.title: Credible set
def-ci-credible.html: Let θ be a function of the parameters and let π(⋅∣y) be its posterior distribution. A set C(y) with Pr{θ∈C(y)∣y}≥1−α is a 1−α credible set for θ. If the posterior has a density π(θ∣y), a set of the form {θ:π(θ∣y)≥k} with posterior probability 1−α is a highest posterior density (HPD) set.

eq-ci-calibration.html: C={x∈R: (Y¯0−β^0−β^1x)2≤t2s2(1m+1n+(x−x¯)2Sxx)}.

eq-ci-ellipsoid.html: 𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟E(Y)={ϕ0∈Rq: (ϕ^−ϕ0)⊤W−1(ϕ^−ϕ0)≤qs2Fα}.

eq-ci-fieller.html: F(Y)={θ0∈R: (a^−θ0b^)2≤t2s2(v11−2θ0v12+θ02v22)}.

eq-ci-new-observation.html: 𝛃Y0=x0⊤β+ε0,ε0∼N(0,σ2),  ε0 independent of Y,

eq-ci-t-interval.html: 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃I(Y)=[λ⊤β^−tn−r,α/2se(λ⊤β^),  λ⊤β^+tn−r,α/2se(λ⊤β^)].

eq-ci-wh-band.html: 𝛃𝛃Pr{|x⊤β^−x⊤β|≤wksx⊤Gx  for all x∈L}=1−α.

exm-ci-assay.title: Calibrating an assay
exm-ci-assay.html:
In a simulated assay, nine standards of concentration 0,1,…,8 are each measured three times (n=27). The fitted line is 0.0338+0.1161x, with s=0.0131 and slope t statistic 118.7. A new specimen is read m=3 times, with mean reading 0.6521. The classical estimate is x^0=5.327, and the 95% calibration interval is (5.184, 5.471) (t25,0.025=2.060). For an assay this precise the delta-method interval, x^0±t(s/|β^1|)1/m+1/n+(x^0−x¯)2/Sxx, agrees to three decimals: (5.184, 5.471).

Now consider a weak assay with the same design, in which the fitted slope is 0.0021 and its t statistic is only 1.67. The mean reading of the standards is 0.0475. A specimen with mean reading 0.0525, close to that mean, gives the whole real line: nothing about its concentration can be concluded. A specimen with mean reading 0.0775 gives two rays, (−∞, −55.3]∪[7.6, ∞): the middle of the scale is excluded, but not extreme concentrations of either sign. Figure 12.5.1 shows both assays.

In 20000 simulated experiments at x0=5.3, both intervals cover in 0.9517 for the precise assay. With the slope three standard errors from zero (β1=0.00335) the Fieller set again covers in 0.9517, since its event involves only the errors, and is bounded in 0.817 of the experiments, close to the power 0.822 of the slope t test; the delta-method interval covers in 0.9827, wastefully. With the slope two standard errors from zero and x0=12, beyond the standards, the Fieller set covers in 0.9528 and the delta-method interval in only 0.9337.

exm-ci-hidden-extrapolation.title: Hidden extrapolation
exm-ci-hidden-extrapolation.html:
Poverty ranges from 8.5% to 21.9% over the 50 states, and single-parent households from 17.9% to 32.8%. A state with poverty 20%, single-parent households 19% and 60% urban is inside every range, but poor with few single parents, a combination absent from the data. Its leverage is h0=0.435, far above the largest leverage among the actual states, 0.260 (Mississippi). Figure 12.3.1 shows the contours of h0 over the two regressors, with urbanization held at its mean.

The fitted rate is 3.817. The 95% interval for the mean is (1.840, 5.794), longer than at the centroid by the factor 0.435/0.0200=4.66. The prediction interval, (0.227, 7.407), is only 1.186 times as long as at the centroid, because it is dominated by s. The prediction interval barely registers the extrapolation, and the real danger, that the model may be wrong where there are no data to check it, is in neither formula. If urbanization is dropped from the model the leverage of this point falls to 0.287, as @prp-ci-new-leverage(c) requires.

exm-ci-stackloss-band.title: A band for the stack loss line
exm-ci-stackloss-band.title_html: A band for the stack loss line
exm-ci-stackloss-band.html:
Regress stack loss on air flow for the 21 days of Brownlee’s plant data (@exm-opt-stackloss-mle), ignoring the other two regressors. The fitted line is −44.132+1.0203x with s=4.098, x¯=60.43 and Sxx=1681.1. The pointwise multiplier is t19,0.025=2.093, and the Working–Hotelling multiplier is 2F0.05(2,19)=2.654, larger by the factor 1.268. Figure 12.4.1 shows the data, the band, the pointwise intervals, and the 95% prediction intervals of Section 12.3.

Near the centre, at x=60, the fitted mean is 17.09, and the half-widths are 1.87 (pointwise), 2.38 (band) and 8.78 (prediction). At x=80, the edge of the data, the fitted mean is 37.49 and the half-widths are 4.50, 5.71 and 9.69.

In 40000 data sets simulated from the fitted line, the band contained the true line over the whole real line in a proportion 0.9500 of the samples and over the observed range 50≤x≤80 in 0.9537. The pointwise intervals covered at x=60 in 0.9517 of the samples, but covered the line over the whole observed range in only 0.8705.

exm-ci-stackloss-predictive.title: Predicting a day of stack loss
exm-ci-stackloss-predictive.title_html: Predicting a day of stack loss
exm-ci-stackloss-predictive.html:
Take the stack loss regression with the engineer’s prior of @exm-opt-stackloss-bayes, and consider a new day with air flow 65, water temperature 23 and acid concentration 87. The posterior has an=13.5, so ν=27 and t27,0.025=2.052. By @thm-ci-bayes-credible, the 95% credible interval for the mean stack loss at these conditions is 23.12±1.51, and the 95% posterior predictive interval for the day’s stack loss is 23.12±6.11. The least squares answers are 23.15±1.77 for the mean and 23.15±7.07 for the new day, with t17,0.025=2.110. The Bayesian intervals are shorter because the prior informs the slopes, shrinking x0⊤Vnx0, and σ2, raising the degrees of freedom from 17 to 27.

The 2.5% and 97.5% points of 400000 posterior predictive draws are 17.00 and 29.21, matching the t interval within Monte Carlo error. The simulated posterior probability of the credible ellipse of (b) for the air-flow and water-temperature coefficients is 0.9503.

exm-ci-state-ellipse.title: A joint region for two coefficients
exm-ci-state-ellipse.title_html: A joint region for two coefficients
exm-ci-state-ellipse.html:
In the murder-rate regression of @exm-ci-state-intervals, take Λ to pick out the coefficients of poverty and single parenthood, so q=2, 𝛟ϕ^=(0.2538, 0.3980)⊤, and the correlation of the two estimates is −0.639. The negative correlation reflects the positive correlation of the regressors: the data can credit murder to either, but not to both at once. With F0.05(2,46)=3.200, the 95% ellipse is drawn in Figure 12.2.1. The F statistic for 𝛟ϕ=0 is 39.81, so the origin is far outside.

The shadows of the ellipse on the two axes are (0.018, 0.490) and (0.188, 0.608), wider than the t intervals (0.066, 0.442) and (0.231, 0.565) by the factor 2×3.200/2.013=1.257. Two points show how the ellipse and the box disagree.

  • A =(0.442, 0.565), the upper corner of the box. Neither t test rejects, but A raises both coefficients at once, against the correlation, and the joint test rejects: F=11.230, p=0.0001.
  • B =(0.463, 0.224), on the long axis of the ellipse. Both t statistics exceed 2.013 (2.242 and 2.098), but B trades one coefficient for the other, which the data cannot resolve, and F=2.888<3.200.

The ellipse and the box have similar areas (0.1197 and 0.1255) but different shapes. In 40000 simulated data sets from the fitted model the ellipse covered the true pair in a proportion 0.9500 and the box in only 0.9164.

exm-ci-state-intervals.title: Murder rates: coefficients and a mean
exm-ci-state-intervals.title_html: Murder rates: coefficients and a mean
exm-ci-state-intervals.html:
Return to the regression of the 2009 murder rate of the 50 states on the poverty rate, the percentage of single-parent households and the percentage urban, with an intercept (@exm-proj-fwl-crime). Here n=50, r=4, s2=2.217, and t46,0.025=2.013. The 95% intervals for the coefficients are

Coefficient Estimate Standard error 95% interval
intercept −9.0946 1.5555 (−12.226, −5.964)
poverty 0.2538 0.0934 (0.066, 0.442)
single parent 0.3980 0.0829 (0.231, 0.565)
urban 0.0046 0.0131 (−0.022, 0.031)

The data are consistent with anything from 0.066 to 0.442 murders per 100,000 for each point of poverty, with the other regressors held fixed in the sense of @thm-proj-fwl. The urban interval straddles zero but is narrow, which says more than “not significant”: any such association is at most 0.031 per percentage point.

A mean response is an estimable function too. For a hypothetical state with poverty 18%, single-parent households 28% and 70% urban, x0=(1,18,28,70)⊤, the estimated mean murder rate is 6.937 with standard error 0.412, and the 95% interval is (6.107, 7.767). Here x0⊤Gx0=0.0767. Section 12.3 interprets this number as the leverage of the new point.

exm-ci-state-prediction.title: Predicting a state’s murder rate
exm-ci-state-prediction.html: In the murder-rate regression, consider a state at the centroid of the regressors. Its leverage is h0=1/n=0.0200 (see @prp-ci-new-leverage), the fitted rate is 4.514, and the 95% intervals are mean response: (4.090, 4.938),new state: (1.487, 7.541). The prediction interval is 7.14 times as long as the interval for the mean, and nearly all of its length, 6.053 per 100,000, comes from s.

exr-ci-band-ellipse.title: B1
exr-ci-band-ellipse.html: For the straight line, show that the Working–Hotelling band contains the line b0+b1x for every x iff (b0,b1) lies in the 1−α confidence ellipse for (β0,β1) of @thm-ci-ellipsoid. Deduce that the band is the envelope of all lines whose coefficients lie in the ellipse.

exr-ci-band-limit.title: A1
exr-ci-band-limit.html: For a straight line with many residual degrees of freedom, compute the ratio of the Working–Hotelling multiplier to the pointwise one at α=0.05. How does the ratio change at α=0.01?

exr-ci-band-quadratic.title: B2
exr-ci-band-quadratic.html: For quadratic regression EYi=β0+β1xi+β2xi2, the natural band over all x uses x=(1,x,x2)⊤, a curve in R3 whose directions do not fill R3. Show that the band with multiplier w3 has coverage at least 1−α over all x, and argue that its coverage is strictly larger than 1−α. (Hint: when is the maximizing direction X⊤v of Step 2 a multiple of some (1,x,x2)⊤?)

exr-ci-band-through-origin.title: A2
exr-ci-band-through-origin.html: For the line through the origin EYi=βxi, show that a simultaneous band for βx over all real x is β^x±tn−1,α/2s|x|/∑xi2, with no widening at all. Explain this with the dimension k of @thm-ci-working-hotelling.

exr-ci-bayes-calibration.title: C2
exr-ci-bayes-calibration.html: In the calibration model of Section 12.5, give x0 a normal prior independent of the regression parameters, and use the flat prior 1/σ2 for (β0,β1,σ2). Write down the posterior density of x0 up to a constant, and show that it is proper even when the slope is not significant. Compare the behaviour of the resulting credible interval with the Fieller set in the weak assay of @exm-ci-assay.

exr-ci-calibration-mle.title: A2
exr-ci-calibration-mle.html: Show that x^0, together with the least squares estimates from the standards, maximizes the joint likelihood of the n+m readings over (β0,β1,σ2,x0) when β^1≠0. What is the maximum likelihood estimate of σ2?

exr-ci-calibration-pooled.title: B1
exr-ci-calibration-pooled.html: When m≥2, the new readings carry their own information about σ2. Let sp2={SSE+∑j(Y0j−Y¯0)2}/(n+m−3). Show that replacing s by sp and tn−2,α/2 by tn+m−3,α/2 in @eq-ci-calibration gives another exact 1−α set. Why is it shorter on average, and why is it more often bounded?

exr-ci-ellipse-difference.title: B2
exr-ci-ellipse-difference.html: In @exm-ci-state-ellipse, the hypothesis that one point of poverty and one point of single parenthood have the same coefficient is the line ϕ1=ϕ2. Using @lem-ci-cauchy-schwarz, show that this line meets the ellipse iff |ϕ^1−ϕ^2|≤2Fα(2,n−r)se(ϕ^1−ϕ^2). Compare this with the t test of ϕ1=ϕ2. Which is appropriate if the hypothesis was formulated before seeing the data?

exr-ci-ellipse-line.title: A2
exr-ci-ellipse-line.html: For the straight line EYi=β0+β1xi, write the 95% confidence ellipse for (β0,β1) in terms of n, x¯ and ∑xi2. Show that in the centred parameterization EYi=γ0+β1(xi−x¯) the axes of the ellipse for (γ0,β1) are parallel to the coordinate axes. When is it a circle?

exr-ci-ellipse-one.title: A1
exr-ci-ellipse-one.html: Show that for q=1 the ellipsoid @eq-ci-ellipsoid is the t interval @eq-ci-t-interval. Which fact about the F(1,ν) distribution does this use?

exr-ci-equivalence.title: B2
exr-ci-equivalence.html: Let δ>0 be a margin below which 𝛌𝛃|λ⊤β| is considered negligible. The two one-sided tests procedure declares equivalence when both 𝛌𝛃H1:λ⊤β≤−δ and 𝛌𝛃H2:λ⊤β≥δ are rejected by one-sided t tests at level α. Show that this happens iff the 1−2α interval @eq-ci-t-interval lies inside (−δ,δ). Show that the procedure has level α: when 𝛌𝛃|λ⊤β|≥δ, the probability of declaring equivalence is at most α.

exr-ci-fieller-geometry.title: C1
exr-ci-fieller-geometry.html: In the setting of @prp-ci-fieller, let 𝛟𝛟𝛟Et={ϕ∈R2:((a^,b^)⊤−ϕ)⊤V−1((a^,b^)⊤−ϕ)≤t2s2}, an ellipse with the t constant in place of 2Fα(2,n−r). Show that θ0∈F(Y) iff the line {(ϕ1,ϕ2):ϕ1=θ0ϕ2} meets Et. Use the picture to explain the three cases: the set is the whole line iff Et contains the origin, and it is bounded iff Et does not meet the axis ϕ2=0.

exr-ci-flat-rank-deficient.title: C1
exr-ci-flat-rank-deficient.html: Let X have rank r<p and take the flat prior 𝛃π(β,σ2)∝1/σ2. Show that the posterior of 𝛃β is improper, but that for estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β the posterior of 𝛌𝛃(λ⊤β,σ2) can be defined by reparameterizing with 𝛄𝛃γ=U⊤β and 𝛅𝛃δ=N⊤β, where the columns of U and N are orthonormal bases of C(X⊤) and N(X), and integrating over nothing but 𝛄γ. Show that the resulting credible interval is the t interval of @thm-ci-estimable-interval with n−r degrees of freedom, provided the flat prior is taken as 1/σ2 in 𝛄(γ,σ2) alone.

exr-ci-g-prior-interval.title: B1
exr-ci-g-prior-interval.html: Under the g-prior of @prp-opt-shrinkage(c) with m0=0, show that the credible interval for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β is centred at 𝛌𝛃{g/(1+g)}λ⊤β^ and has half-width 𝛌𝛌tν,α/2τg/(1+g)λ⊤(X⊤X)−1λ. Compare it with the t interval as g→∞, paying attention to ν and τ2.

exr-ci-hpd-sigma.title: A1
exr-ci-hpd-sigma.html: Is the equal-tailed interval of @thm-ci-bayes-credible(d) the HPD interval for σ2? Describe the HPD interval and explain the difference.

exr-ci-intersection.title: C2
exr-ci-intersection.html: Two straight lines EY=αk+βkx, k=1,2, are fitted to two independent samples in one model with a common σ2, as in a two-phase regression. Use @prp-ci-fieller to construct a confidence set for the x-coordinate (α1−α2)/(β2−β1) of their intersection. When is it bounded? Interpret the unbounded cases in terms of parallel lines.

exr-ci-inverse-estimator.title: B3
exr-ci-inverse-estimator.html:
Study the two estimators of the Remark “Classical or inverse estimation?” in an idealized large calibration experiment: the standards are so numerous that β^0, β^1 and R2 may be replaced by constants β0, β1≠0 and ρ2∈(0,1), while Y¯0 is still the mean of m new readings. Let v=σ2/(mβ12).

  1. Show that x^0 is unbiased with mean squared error v, and that x~0=x¯+ρ2(x^0−x¯) has mean squared error ρ4v+(1−ρ2)2(x0−x¯)2.
  2. Show that x~0 has the smaller mean squared error iff (x0−x¯)2<v(1+ρ2)/(1−ρ2).
  3. Let τ2=Sxx/n, so that in this limit ρ2=β12τ2/(β12τ2+σ2). Show that the condition of part 2 reads (x0−x¯)2<v+2τ2/m. With m=1 and a precise instrument, roughly how far from x¯, in units of the spread τ of the standards, does the inverse estimator stay ahead?

exr-ci-joint-predictive.title: B2
exr-ci-joint-predictive.html: Two future observations are taken at the same x0. Show that, under the posterior predictive distribution, they are correlated, and find the correlation. Why are they correlated when their errors are independent? Are they independent under the frequentist model?

exr-ci-kappa.title: B1
exr-ci-kappa.html: Show that κν→1 as ν→∞, and that s/κn−r is an unbiased estimator of σ. Compute κν for ν=1 and ν=2.

exr-ci-known-covariance.title: B3
exr-ci-known-covariance.html: Suppose 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2V) with V known and positive definite and X of full column rank. Using the generalized least squares estimator 𝛃β~=(X⊤V−1X)−1X⊤V−1Y and 𝛃𝛃s~2=(Y−Xβ~)⊤V−1(Y−Xβ~)/(n−p), derive an exact 1−α interval for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β. Write it out for a straight line EYi=β0+β1xi with V=diag(1/wi).

exr-ci-leverage-increment.title: B2
exr-ci-leverage-increment.html: In @prp-ci-new-leverage(c), let X have full column rank and add a single column z∉C(X). Show that the new leverage is h0+=h0+(z0−k⊤x0)2‖(I−M)z‖2,k=(X⊤X)−1X⊤z. So the leverage is unchanged iff z0 equals the value k⊤x0 predicted for it by the other regressors.

exr-ci-likelihood-region.title: C1
exr-ci-likelihood-region.html: Let X have full column rank. Show that the confidence ellipsoid for 𝛃β is a region of the form 𝛃{b: ℓp(b)≥ℓp(β^)−k}, where ℓp(b)=maxσ2ℓ(b,σ2) is the profile log-likelihood of Chapter 7, and find k in terms of Fα(p,n−p). How does k compare with the value 12χα2(p) suggested by the asymptotic theory of likelihood ratios?

exr-ci-oneway-contrast.title: B4
exr-ci-oneway-contrast.html: In a one-way layout with a groups of sizes n1,…,na and the overparameterized model EYij=μ+αi, show that the interval for α1−α2 is y¯1⋅−y¯2⋅±tn−a,α/2s1/n1+1/n2, with n=∑ni. What does @prp-ci-nonestimable say about an interval for α1 alone?

exr-ci-pi-ratio.title: A1
exr-ci-pi-ratio.html: Show that the ratio of the length of the prediction interval to that of the confidence interval for the mean at x0 is (1+h0)/h0. What is it in @exm-ci-state-prediction, and what happens to it as n→∞ with the design growing regularly?

exr-ci-prediction-band.title: C1
exr-ci-prediction-band.html: A single new observation 𝛃Y0=x0⊤β+ε0 will be taken at a regressor vector x0∈C(X⊤) that is not known in advance. Show that the band 𝛃x⊤β^±(r+1)Fα(r+1,n−r)s1+x⊤Gx, x∈C(X⊤), contains Y0 with probability at least 1−α, whatever x0 turns out to be. (Hint: apply Step 2 of the proof to the (r+1)-dimensional vector (v,ε0).)

exr-ci-predictive-moments.title: A2
exr-ci-predictive-moments.html: For ν>2, find the posterior predictive mean and variance of a single future observation at x0. Why is the variance larger than τ2(1+x0⊤Vnx0)?

exr-ci-random-x0.title: B4
exr-ci-random-x0.html: Suppose the new regressor vector X0 is random, independent of the pair (Y,ε0), and always lies in C(X⊤). Show that the prediction interval of @thm-ci-prediction-interval, computed at the realized X0, still covers Y0 with probability exactly 1−α.

exr-ci-replicate.title: A1
exr-ci-replicate.html: A design is replicated m times: X is replaced by m stacked copies of itself. For a fixed estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β, how does 𝛌𝛌λ⊤Gλ change? Roughly how many replicates are needed to halve the expected length of the 95% interval when n−r is already large, and why is the answer slightly less than 4 when n−r is small?

exr-ci-shortest-sigma.title: C2
exr-ci-shortest-sigma.html: Intervals for σ2 of the form [SSE/c2, SSE/c1] with Pr(c1≤χ2(ν)≤c2)=1−α all have exact coverage. Show that the one with the smallest expected length satisfies c12f(c1)=c22f(c2), where f is the χ2(ν) density, and that the equal-tailed choice of @prp-ci-sigma does not satisfy this condition.

exr-ci-shortest-t.title: C1
exr-ci-shortest-t.html: Among intervals 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃[λ⊤β^−ase, λ⊤β^+bse] with a,b≥0 and coverage exactly 1−α, show that the expected length is smallest when a=b=tn−r,α/2. (Use that the t density is symmetric and strictly decreasing in |x|.)

exr-ci-simultaneous-prediction.title: C1
exr-ci-simultaneous-prediction.html: Let k new observations be made at the rows of a k×p matrix X0 whose rows lie in C(X⊤), with errors independent of each other and of Y. Show that 𝛃D=Y0−X0β^∼Nk(0,σ2(Ik+X0GX0⊤)), independent of s2, and deduce that the intervals 𝛃x0j⊤β^ ± kFα(k,n−r) s1+h0j,j=1,…,k, contain all k new observations simultaneously with probability at least 1−α.

exr-ci-singular-lambda.title: B3
exr-ci-singular-lambda.html: Let the columns of Λ lie in C(X⊤) but be linearly dependent, with rank(Λ)=k<q. Show that W=Λ⊤GΛ is singular, that 𝛟𝛟ϕ^−ϕ∈C(W) with probability one, and that 𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟{ϕ0∈ϕ^+C(W): (ϕ^−ϕ0)⊤W−(ϕ^−ϕ0)≤ks2Fα(k,n−r)} is an exact 1−α confidence set, a k-dimensional ellipsoid inside a k-dimensional affine subspace of Rq.

exr-ci-stationary.title: B2
exr-ci-stationary.html: In the quadratic regression EYi=β0+β1xi+β2xi2, use @prp-ci-fieller to give a confidence set for the location x∗=−β1/(2β2) of the turning point. When is it a bounded interval, and what does that condition mean for the curvature?

exr-ci-through-origin.title: B3
exr-ci-through-origin.html: For the line through the origin, EYi=βxi with ∑xi2>0, write the 1−α confidence interval for the mean at x0 and the prediction interval for Y0. Show that the confidence interval for the mean has length proportional to |x0|, and is a point at x0=0. Why is that reasonable, and what does it assume?

exr-ci-tolerance.title: C2
exr-ci-tolerance.html: A (P,1−α) tolerance interval at x0 is a random interval that, with probability at least 1−α over Y, contains at least a proportion P of the distribution of Y0. Show that the prediction interval of @thm-ci-prediction-interval is not a (1−α,1−α) tolerance interval, by showing that its conditional coverage given Y is below 1−α with probability bounded away from zero. Construct a conservative tolerance interval from a lower confidence bound for the conditional coverage, using a 1−α/2 upper confidence bound for σ and a 1−α/2 confidence interval for 𝛃x0⊤β.

exr-ci-two-bands.title: C2
exr-ci-two-bands.html: Two straight lines are fitted in one model, with separate intercepts and slopes and a common σ2. Construct simultaneous bands for both lines with joint coverage at least 1−α in two ways: (i) @thm-ci-working-hotelling with L=R4, (ii) a band for each line with L=R2 at level α/2, combined by the Bonferroni inequality. Compare the multipliers for n−r=20 and explain which is better and why.

exr-ci-two-future.title: B1
exr-ci-two-future.html: Two new observations will be made, at x01 and x02, with independent errors. Find an exact 1−α prediction interval for their difference Y01−Y02. Show that when x01=x02 it does not depend on the data except through s.

exr-ci-volume-ratio.title: B1
exr-ci-volume-ratio.html: Take q=2 and let ρ be the correlation of ϕ^1 and ϕ^2. Show that the area of the ellipse divided by the area of the box of the two t intervals is πFα(2,n−r)2tn−r,α/221−ρ2, so that it depends on the design only through ρ. Check it against @exm-ci-state-ellipse, where the areas are 0.1197 and 0.1255 at ρ=−0.639. For which |ρ| do the two regions have equal area there, and what happens to the ratio as the two regressors become collinear?

exr-ci-x-intercept.title: A1
exr-ci-x-intercept.html: For a straight line, write down Fieller’s 1−α confidence set for the point ξ=−β0/β1 where the line crosses zero, and state the condition under which it is a bounded interval. Show that it is the calibration set of @thm-ci-calibration with Y¯0 replaced by 0 and 1/m replaced by 0.

lem-ci-cauchy-schwarz.title: Extent of an ellipsoid
lem-ci-cauchy-schwarz.html: Let W be a q×q positive definite matrix and c>0. For every a∈Rq, max{a⊤u: u⊤W−1u≤c}=ca⊤Wa, attained at u=c/(a⊤Wa)Wa when a≠0. Consequently u⊤W−1u≤c iff |a⊤u|≤ca⊤Wa for every a∈Rq.

lem-ci-mvt.title: Multivariate t
lem-ci-mvt.title_html: Multivariate t
lem-ci-mvt.html:
Let u∼tν(m,S) in Rp, with S positive definite.

  1. If A is q×p of rank q, then Au∼tν(Am,ASA⊤).

  2. (u−m)⊤S−1(u−m)/p∼F(p,ν).

  3. u has density proportional to {1+(u−m)⊤S−1(u−m)/ν}−(ν+p)/2.

prp-ci-average-coverage.title: Coverage averaged over the prior
prp-ci-average-coverage.html: Let the prior π be proper, and let C(y) be a 1−α credible set for θ for every y. If 𝛃(β,σ2) is drawn from π and then Y from the model, Pr{θ∈C(Y)}≥1−α, with equality if every C(y) has posterior probability exactly 1−α. Equivalently, the frequentist coverage 𝛃Prβ,σ2{θ∈C(Y)}, averaged over π, is at least 1−α.

prp-ci-calibration-unbounded.title: Unbounded calibration sets cannot be avoided
prp-ci-calibration-unbounded.title_html: Unbounded calibration sets cannot be avoided
prp-ci-calibration-unbounded.html: Let D be any confidence set for x0 with coverage at least 1−α>0 at every parameter value, including those with β1=0. Then at every parameter value with β1=0, Pr{v∈D}≥1−α for every real v, and if D is measurable in the sense of @prp-ci-nonestimable, its expected length is infinite.

prp-ci-duality.title: Tests and confidence sets
prp-ci-duality.html: For each θ0∈Θ, let A(θ0) be the acceptance region of a test of H:θ=θ0 with 𝛃Prβ,σ2{Y∈A(θ0)}≥1−α whenever 𝛃g(β,σ2)=θ0. Then C(y)={θ0∈Θ:y∈A(θ0)} is a 1−α confidence set for θ, and it is exact if every test has size exactly α at every parameter value in its hypothesis. Conversely, if C is a 1−α confidence set, the rule “reject H:θ=θ0 iff θ0∉C(y)” is a level-α test for every θ0.

prp-ci-fieller.title: Fieller’s confidence set for a ratio
prp-ci-fieller.title_html: Fieller’s confidence set for a ratio
prp-ci-fieller.html:
Let 𝛌𝛌λ1,λ2∈C(X⊤) be linearly independent, put 𝛌𝛃a=λ1⊤β, 𝛌𝛃b=λ2⊤β, their estimates 𝛌𝛃a^=λ1⊤β^, 𝛌𝛃b^=λ2⊤β^, and 𝛌𝛌vij=λi⊤Gλj, so that V=(vij) is positive definite. Suppose b≠0 and let θ=a/b. With t=tn−r,α/2, let F(Y)={θ0∈R: (a^−θ0b^)2≤t2s2(v11−2θ0v12+θ02v22)}.{#eq-ci-fieller}

  1. F(Y) is an exact 1−α confidence set for θ, at every parameter value with b≠0.

  2. Let Q=(a^,b^)V−1(a^,b^)⊤. Outside an event of probability zero, F(Y) is

    • a bounded closed interval containing θ^=a^/b^, if b^2>t2s2v22;
    • the union of two disjoint closed rays, if b^2<t2s2v22 and Q>t2s2;
    • the whole real line, if b^2<t2s2v22 and Q<t2s2.

prp-ci-mean-ball.title: Confidence ball for the mean vector
prp-ci-mean-ball.title_html: Confidence ball for the mean vector
prp-ci-mean-ball.html: Let 𝛍𝛃μ=Xβ and cr=rs2Fα(r,n−r). The set 𝛍𝛍B(Y)={μ0∈C(X): ‖Y^−μ0‖2≤cr} is an exact 1−α confidence set for 𝛍μ: a ball of radius cr in the r-dimensional space C(X), centred at the fitted vector. Moreover, if Λ=X⊤T for an n×q matrix T (such a T exists by @thm-est-characterization), the image of B(Y) under 𝛍𝛍μ0↦T⊤μ0 is the set 𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟{ϕ0: (ϕ^−ϕ0)⊤W−1(ϕ^−ϕ0)≤cr}, which contains the ellipsoid @eq-ci-ellipsoid.

prp-ci-new-leverage.title: Leverage of a new point
prp-ci-new-leverage.html:
Let 𝛒x0=X⊤ρ∈C(X⊤) and h0=x0⊤Gx0.

  1. h0=min{‖a‖2: X⊤a=x0}, and the minimum is attained only at 𝛒a=Mρ.

  2. If X=[1,X1] has full column rank, x0=(1,x01⊤)⊤, x¯ is the vector of column means of X1 and X~1=X1−1x¯⊤, then h0=1n+(x01−x¯)⊤(X~1⊤X~1)−1(x01−x¯).

  3. If further columns are added, X+=[X,Z], and x0+=(x0⊤,z0⊤)⊤∈C(X+⊤), then the leverage of x0+ in the enlarged model is at least h0.

prp-ci-nonestimable.title: No useful interval for a non-estimable function
prp-ci-nonestimable.title_html: No useful interval for a non-estimable function
prp-ci-nonestimable.html: Let 𝛌λ∉C(X⊤) and let C be a 1−α confidence set for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β with α<1. Then at every parameter value 𝛃(β,σ2) and for every real v, 𝛃Prβ,σ2{v∈C(Y)}≥1−α. If the sets C(y) are such that {(y,v):v∈C(y)} is measurable, the expected length of C(Y) is infinite at every parameter value.

prp-ci-pi-limit.title: Prediction intervals without normality
prp-ci-pi-limit.html: Consider a sequence of full-rank models 𝛃𝛆Yn=Xnβ+εn with p fixed and n→∞, and a fixed x0 whose leverage h0,n=x0⊤(Xn⊤Xn)−1x0 tends to zero. Let ε1,…,εn and ε0 be independent and identically distributed with mean 0, variance σ2, finite fourth moment and a continuous distribution function, and let 𝛃Y0=x0⊤β+ε0. Then the coverage of the nominal 1−α prediction interval Y^0±tn−p,α/2s1+h0,n satisfies Pr{|Y0−Y^0|≤tn−p,α/2s1+h0,n}⟶ Pr{|ε0|≤zα/2σ}, where zα/2 is the upper α/2 point of N(0,1). Likewise the probabilities of missing above and below tend to Pr{ε0>zα/2σ} and Pr{ε0<−zα/2σ}.

prp-ci-ratio-no-mean.title: The classical estimator has no mean
prp-ci-ratio-no-mean.title_html: The classical estimator has no mean
prp-ci-ratio-no-mean.html: If Pr(Y¯0≠Y¯)>0, which always holds here, then E|x^0|=∞.

prp-ci-sigma.title: Interval for the error variance
prp-ci-sigma.html: The interval [ SSEχα/22(n−r) , SSEχ1−α/22(n−r) ] is an exact 1−α confidence interval for σ2, and the square roots of its endpoints give one for σ.

thm-ci-bayes-credible.title: Credible sets and posterior predictive distribution
thm-ci-bayes-credible.title_html: Credible sets and posterior predictive distribution
thm-ci-bayes-credible.html:
Let the prior be NIG(m0,V0,a0,b0), so that by @thm-opt-bayes-conjugate the posterior is NIG(mn,Vn,an,bn). Put ν=2an and τ2=bn/an.

  1. For 𝛌λ≠0, the interval 𝛌𝛌𝛌λ⊤mn ± tν,α/2τλ⊤Vnλ is the 1−α HPD credible interval for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β; it is also equal-tailed.

  2. For a p×q matrix Λ of rank q, the set 𝛟𝛟𝛟{ϕ0: (ϕ0−Λ⊤mn)⊤(Λ⊤VnΛ)−1(ϕ0−Λ⊤mn)≤qτ2Fα(q,ν)} is the 1−α HPD credible region for 𝛃Λ⊤β.

  3. Let 𝛃𝛆Y0=X0β+ε0 be k future observations, with 𝛆ε0∼Nk(0,σ2Ik) independent of Y and of 𝛃β given σ2. The posterior predictive distribution of Y0 is Y0∣y ∼ tν(X0mn, τ2(Ik+X0VnX0⊤)). In particular, for one future observation at x0, the interval x0⊤mn±tν,α/2τ1+x0⊤Vnx0 has posterior predictive probability 1−α.

  4. [2bn/χα/22(ν), 2bn/χ1−α/22(ν)] is an equal-tailed 1−α credible interval for σ2.

thm-ci-calibration.title: Calibration set
thm-ci-calibration.html:
In the calibration model, let t=tn−2,α/2 and C={x∈R: (Y¯0−β^0−β^1x)2≤t2s2(1m+1n+(x−x¯)2Sxx)}.{#eq-ci-calibration}

  1. C is an exact 1−α confidence set for x0, at every (β0,β1,σ2,x0), including β1=0.

  2. C is the set of x at which Y¯0 lies inside the 1−α prediction interval of @thm-ci-prediction-interval(c) for the mean of m new readings at x.

  3. Let T1=β^1Sxx/s be the t statistic for the slope and g=Y¯0−Y¯. Outside an event of probability zero, C is

    • a bounded interval containing x^0, if T12>t2;
    • the union of two disjoint closed rays, if T12<t2 and T12+g2/{s2(1/m+1/n)}>t2;
    • the whole real line, if T12+g2/{s2(1/m+1/n)}<t2.

thm-ci-ellipsoid.title: Confidence ellipsoid for \bLambda\T\bbeta
thm-ci-ellipsoid.title_html: Confidence ellipsoid for 𝛃Λ⊤β
thm-ci-ellipsoid.html:
With the notation above, let Fα=Fα(q,n−r) and 𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟𝛟E(Y)={ϕ0∈Rq: (ϕ^−ϕ0)⊤W−1(ϕ^−ϕ0)≤qs2Fα}.{#eq-ci-ellipsoid}

  1. E(Y) is an exact 1−α confidence set for 𝛃Λ⊤β.

  2. E(Y) is a solid ellipsoid centred at 𝛟ϕ^. If W=∑k=1qwkukuk⊤ is a spectral decomposition, its principal axes point along u1,…,uq and have half-lengths qs2Fαwk. Its volume is πq/2Γ(q/2+1)(qs2Fα)q/2det(W)1/2.

  3. (Duality with the F test.) For d∈Rq, let SSEd be the minimum of ‖Y−Xb‖2 over {b:Λ⊤b=d} and let 𝛟𝛟Fd=(SSEd−SSE)/qs2=(ϕ^−d)⊤W−1(ϕ^−d)qs2. Then d∈E(Y) iff Fd≤Fα, that is, iff the level-α F test of 𝛃H:Λ⊤β=d does not reject.

thm-ci-estimable-interval.title: The t interval for an estimable function
thm-ci-estimable-interval.title_html: The t interval for an estimable function
thm-ci-estimable-interval.html:
Let 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤), 𝛌λ≠0, and put 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌se(λ⊤β^)=sλ⊤Gλ. Let 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃I(Y)=[λ⊤β^−tn−r,α/2se(λ⊤β^),  λ⊤β^+tn−r,α/2se(λ⊤β^)].{#eq-ci-t-interval}

  1. I(Y) does not depend on the choice of 𝛃β^ or of G.

  2. I(Y) is an exact 1−α confidence interval for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β.

  3. Its length 𝛌𝛌L=2tn−r,α/2sλ⊤Gλ has expectation 𝛌𝛌EL=2tn−r,α/2κn−rσλ⊤Gλ, where κν=EV/ν=2νΓ((ν+1)/2)Γ(ν/2)<1,V∼χ2(ν).

  4. The one-sided intervals 𝛌𝛃(−∞, λ⊤β^+tn−r,αse] and 𝛌𝛃[λ⊤β^−tn−r,αse, ∞) are exact 1−α confidence intervals for 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β.

thm-ci-prediction-interval.title: Prediction interval
thm-ci-prediction-interval.html:
Under @eq-ci-new-observation, put 𝛃Y^0=x0⊤β^.

  1. Y0−Y^0∼N(0,σ2(1+h0)), it is independent of s2, and Y0−Y^0s1+h0∼t(n−r).

  2. The interval Y^0±tn−r,α/2s1+h0 contains Y0 with probability exactly 1−α, the probability being computed over Y and Y0 jointly, at every 𝛃(β,σ2).

  3. More generally, if Y¯0 is the mean of m independent new observations at x0, each distributed as in @eq-ci-new-observation, then Y^0±tn−r,α/2s1/m+h0 contains Y¯0 with probability exactly 1−α. As m→∞ this interval becomes the confidence interval Y^0±tn−r,α/2sh0 for 𝛃x0⊤β.

thm-ci-working-hotelling.title: Working–Hotelling band
thm-ci-working-hotelling.html:
Let L be a linear subspace of C(X⊤) of dimension k≥1, and let wk=kFα(k,n−r). Then 𝛃𝛃Pr{|x⊤β^−x⊤β|≤wksx⊤Gx  for all x∈L}=1−α.{#eq-ci-wh-band}

In particular:

  1. with L=C(X⊤) and k=r, the functions 𝛃x⊤β^±wrsx⊤Gx form an exact 1−α simultaneous band for the regression surface over all estimable x;

  2. for a straight line EYi=β0+β1xi with the xi not all equal, the band β^0+β^1x ± 2Fα(2,n−2) s1n+(x−x¯)2Sxx,x∈R, contains the true line β0+β1x for every real x with probability exactly 1−α.
